title: Jackie Robinson, the first African American in Major League Baseball since the 1880s, signs a contract with the Brooklyn Dodgers.
text: The Brooklyn Dodgers were a Major League Baseball team founded in 1883 as the Brooklyn Grays. In 1884, it became a member of the American Association as the Brooklyn Atlantics before joining the National League in 1890.

title: Paul I becomes King of Greece, aged 45, following the death of his brother, King George II.
text: Paul was King of Greece from 1 April 1947 until his death on 6 March 1964. Paul was born at Tatoi Palace as the third son of Crown Prince Constantine and Crown Princess Sophia of Greece.

title: The 1947 Royal New Zealand Navy mutinies begin.
text: During April 1947, the Royal New Zealand Navy experienced a series of non-violent mutinies amongst the enlisted sailors of four ships and two shore bases. Over 20 per cent of the RNZN's enlisted personnel were punished or discharged for their involvement.

title: The International Civil Aviation Organization begins operations.
text: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations that coordinates the principles and techniques of international air navigation, and fosters the planning and development of international air transport to ensure safe and orderly growth. The ICAO headquarters are in the Quartier international de Montréal of Montreal, Quebec, Canada.
